headline: High: Mem0 can feed MemMachine via MCP/REST with no isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content through a shared channel. Mem0 is a knowledge-management memory layer with no isolation or provenance controls shown, so if its outputs are routed into MemMachine, attacker-controlled memory text can be treated as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Mem0 outputs are forwarded into MemMachine via MCP or REST
IF MemMachine parses retrieved memory text as instructions or tool directives
IF no provenance or instruction/content separation is added
mitigations: Add a strict content/instruction delimiter in the bridge
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted memory records
Require provenance tags on all Mem0-sourced text
Review one end-to-end sample before enabling automation
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing and policy enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress over allowlisted network paths. Mem0 is a memory store with no documented data-class limits or isolation, so shared use can move sensitive context from Mem0 into MemMachine outputs or API calls. The leakage path is plausible, but the profiles do not show uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF Mem0 stores sensitive user facts that MemMachine later retrieves
IF MemMachine sends retrieved context through its allowlisted egress
IF both agents are connected to the same workspace or memory corpus
mitigations: Restrict Mem0 to non-sensitive records
Turn off MemMachine egress for memory-backed requests
Separate workspaces for the two agents
Inspect one sample payload for sensitive fields before rollout
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 shows no write or network surface beyond none, while MemMachine has allowlisted egress and MCP/API access. There is no evidence both agents write the same mutable resource or share overlapping write scopes, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not expose a shared writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same filesystem or database
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable workspace
IF Mem0 gains write capabilities not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate storage paths
Avoid shared git or database writes
Document ownership of each mutable resource
Check current permissions before enabling collaboration
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can consume Mem0-derived memory through MCP or API flows, and nothing in either profile shows a verification step. That makes Mem0's stored facts a plausible authoritative input to MemMachine's travel-planning outputs, creating a cascade if stale or incorrect memories are rendered into actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses Mem0 output as authoritative memory
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks retrieved facts
IF downstream actions are generated from those facts
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on memory
Show source snippets alongside retrieved facts
Limit automation to suggestions, not actions
Spot-check one generated itinerary for factual drift
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and source validation

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while Mem0 is a memory system with no residency, retention, or certification claims shown. The profiles do not show a concrete jurisdiction or regulated data class mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documented-policy gaps rather than a clear breach. Only MemMachine is cited because the mismatch is not specified for Mem0.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Mem0 or MemMachine
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two systems
IF a jurisdictional restriction applies to the transferred data
mitigations: Confirm retention settings on both systems
Avoid placing regulated data in shared memory
Document deletion/export handling for memory records
Review jurisdiction before enabling cross-system sync
requires-engineering: align policy enforcement across both agents
